proposed_from.topic: Sound-and-complete lagged micro-effect identification from latent-confounded summary time-series graphs. Fix a finite observed coordinate set, lag bound L, directed/bidirected summary H, X,Y,gamma and x. Quantify over every positive finite-alphabet strictly stationary order-L time-homogeneous semi-Markovian SCM with acyclic instantaneous slices and exact summary H. Construct a terminating graph-native TID-SCG procedure that either outputs one finite-cylinder do-free functional valid for every compatible SCM or a finite lag-switch-hedge certificate constructing two compatible stationary SCMs with the same entire observed process law and unequal P(Y_0|do(X_-gamma=x)). Prove soundness, completeness and an explicit termination bound through a lag-robust intrinsic-district transducer; refinement enumeration, generic QE and tautological model gluing do not qualify. Add cylinder plug-in and HAC delta-method inference under positivity and geometric beta-mixing. Consumer: EasyRCA lag-specific anomaly-transmission ranking under hidden confounding. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An independent-shift construction preserves whole-process observational equality, intervention separation, lag bounds, positivity and exact summaries when lifting finite collisions; an acyclic directed-summary subclass reduces to one ordinary ID call on at most n(nL+1) ancestral vertices. The repaired XOR witness gives 19/50 versus 31/50, and a separate positive stationary lag-switch pair has identical observed process laws but effects 13/50 versus 1/2. Checks show raw quotienting need not preserve fixability and per-refinement ID is insufficient. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a bounded uniform fixing normal form whose states either compile one universal finite-cylinder arithmetic functional or extract two positive temporal-role SCMs, including disagreement between individually identifiable refinements. EARLY KILL TEST: For |V|<=3 and L=1, test the proposed states and rewrites on the front-door witness, the offset-sensitive fixing counterexample and the stationary lag-switch pair; pivot if the procedure accepts the collision, rejects front-door, conflates offsets or needs unrestricted elimination. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The exact gap is uniform micro-effect identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with \(\mathcal A\) fixed so its members share \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) while differing in temporal vertices, ancestral margins, intrinsic districts, and instantaneous orders. Causally sufficient SCG total-effect adjustment is already addressed by Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui, and causally sufficient linear direct-effect completeness by Ferreira--Assaad; neither model contains hidden common causes or requires district fixing. Assaad's Theorem 1 admits latent confounding but supplies one sufficient front-door configuration rather than a generic front-door frontier or a general necessity and failure certificate. Ferreira--Assaad's macro completeness acts on whole time-series clusters rather than one variable at lag \(\gamma\). Shpitser--Pearl and Richardson--Robins--Evans--Shpitser fix one finite ADMG, Jahn--Karnik--Schulman fix one periodic fine graph, and Jaber and coauthors fix the vertices and Markov-equivalence representation of one PAG. None detects a collision in which each temporal refinement is identifiable but the valid functionals disagree on a common positive stationary law in \(\mathcal P(\Omega_{\mathcal A})\). The new mathematical object is the lag-robust intrinsic-district state carrying temporal offsets and a typed kernel identity across admissible refinements. The new necessity argument must localize every uniform failure to a finite lag-switch hedge and use independent shifts to construct two positive, time-homogeneous, exact-summary stationary SCMs in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with the same entire observed process law on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). The sole strict comparator promise is a generic-class frontier: every certificate in the explicit family \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}\) maps to TID-SCG success, Assaad's published criterion is a proved member, and the lag-one witness \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\) lies outside the family yet succeeds through the complete trace \(\mathfrak t_{\mathrm{out}}\). Generic refinement enumeration, real quantifier elimination, and semantic branch gluing do not deliver these objects and are outside the kernel.

proposed_from.literature_map: Shpitser and Pearl (2008) supply the fixed-ADMG recursive ID and hedge benchmark. Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser (2023) express hidden-variable constraints and effect identification through reachable intrinsic sets and fixing kernels. Assaad (2025) is the closest micro-effect paper: Theorem 1 composes two uniformly valid intervention kernels under sufficient SCG front-door conditions, and the concluding discussion does not provide completeness. Ferreira and Assaad (2025) prove macro, not micro, do-calculus completeness for latent-confounded SCGs. Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier (2025) give necessary and sufficient common-adjustment conditions under causal sufficiency. Yvernes and coauthors (2025) separate graphwise identification, common proof, and common-functional criteria. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022) provide a complete possible-c-component region recursion over the finite graphs represented by a PAG. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025) prove a bounded-segment theorem for one fully specified periodic graph by cutting repeated hedge signatures; unknown summary refinements and common arithmetic outputs are outside their result. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022) compile fixed-graph identifying functionals into estimators under independent sampling. Viviano and Bradic (2023) establish causal testing under stationary beta mixing for a different synthetic-control target, and Newey and West (1987) provide the HAC template. Duarte and coauthors (2024) reduce fixed discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs, which is adjacent but excluded as the proposed graph-native mechanism. EasyRCA (Assaad, Ez-zejjari, and Zan, 2023) compares regime-specific direct effects under independent noises and names hidden common causes as an extension boundary.
